title: Stone LLM concept
abstract: notes Based on the indexed array of objects in the stone programming paradigm , stone method from travis raymond-charlie stone on zenodo mapping each word in the dictionary and adding the thesaurus in a heap to make a trie structure control the output in the most likely answer to the prompt, an efficient algorithm is possible A Trie is a data structure that can be used to efficiently manage and search through sequences of tokens, making it suitable for controlling large language models (LLMs) during text generation. By organizing tokens in a tree-like structure, a Trie allows for quick prefix-based searches, which is beneficial for applications like auto-complete and search suggestions. “LLM as a trie” can mean two related ideas: Using a trie to constrain an LLM’s output Thinking of an LLM’s language knowledgeas if it were a trie The first is technically useful; the second is mostly an analogy. A trie, or prefix tree, stores sequences by sharing their prefixes. For example, these phrases: could be represented as: At each point, the trie tells you which next symbols are valid. For an LLM, the symbols are usually tokens, not individual characters. Suppose an application only allows these outputs: After the model generates the token sequence corresponding to "gr", the trie can restrict the next token to one that continues "green". Any token that would produce an invalid phrase is masked before sampling. Conceptually, generation becomes: Pconstrained(t∣x)={PLLM(t∣x),if t is allowed by the trie0,otherwise The remaining probabilities are then renormalized. This is useful for: Autocomplete: only suggest completions ina known vocabulary. Entity linking: generate only valid namesfrom a database. Classification: force the answer to be oneof a fixed set of labels. Structured generation: restrict values tovalid keys, commands, or identifiers. Retrieval systems: efficiently search a largecollection of tokenized phrases. Security-sensitive interfaces: preventgeneration of unsupported commands. A simple character-level implementation might look like this: With an LLM, the same idea is applied to token IDs. During every generation step: Take the tokens generated so far. Find the corresponding node in the trie. Determine the valid next token IDs. Set the logits of all other tokens to negativeinfinity. Sample or select the next token. In practice, there are complications: A word may consist of several subwordtokens. Token boundaries may include spaces orpunctuation. The same text can sometimes have multipletokenizations. A trie may need to store token sequencesrather than strings. If the model generates an invalid token,recovery may require backtracking. Very large tries can consume substantialmemory. An LLM itself is not literally a trie. A trie stores explicit sequences and supports exact prefix lookup. An LLM stores statistical patterns in neural-network weights. It can generalize to phrases it has never seen, while a trie can only follow paths that were inserted into it. A useful comparison is: Trie: “Which continuations are explicitlyallowed?” LLM: “Which continuation is statisticallylikely?” Together: “Which allowed continuation ismost likely?” This combination is often called constrained decoding or grammar-guided generation. A trie works well for finite lists, while grammars, regular expressions, JSON schemas, and parser states are better for more complex structures. Based on the indexed array of objects in the stone programming paradigm , stone method from travis raymond-charlie stone on zenodo mapping each word in the dictionary and adding the thesaurus in a heap to make a trie structure control the output in the most likely answer to the prompt, an efficient algorithm is possible an efficient algorithm is possible, but the trie should be used as a candidate-generation and output-constraint layer, not as a replacement for the language model. The Stone materials describe lookup-oriented structures, indexed variables, parallel string/integer handling, and shifting computation from open-ended evaluation toward precomputed lookup. That maps naturally onto a symbolic language pipeline: dictionary entries become indexed objects, related words become adjacency lists, and the trie represents valid token or word prefixes. A practical architecture would be: Each dictionary object could contain more than a word: The trie would index the token sequence: The thesaurus should not simply substitute every word with every synonym. Instead, it should produce weighted alternatives. For a query word w w, define a candidate score such as: S(c∣w,x)=αPLLM(c∣x)+βRsemantic(c,w)+γF(c)+δC(c,x)−λD(c,w) S(c∣w,x)=αP (c∣x)+βR (c,w)+γF(c)+δC(c,x)−λD(c,w) where: PLLMP is the model’s probability forcandidate cc, RsemanticR measures thesaurus orembedding similarity, F(c)F(c) is frequency or reliability, C(c,x)C(c,x) measures compatibility with theprompt context, D(c,w)D(c,w) penalizes overly distantsubstitutions. A max-heap can retain the best partial paths during search. For example, beam search over the trie can be written as: This produces a trie-guided beam search. The trie removes impossible continuations, while the heap keeps the most promising valid continuations. If the trie contains only approved words or phrases, the output can be guaranteed to belong to that vocabulary. For efficiency, several optimizations matter: Store integer token IDs rather than stringsinside trie edges. Use an array-based or compact double-array trie for cache-friendly lookup. Store synonym links as integer IDs into aseparate array. Keep only the top kk thesaurus relations perword. Cache trie nodes reached by commonprefixes. Batch model scoring for multiple candidatepaths. Use beam search rather than exploring theentire tree. Quantize or precompute static scores wherepossible. Separate immutable dictionary data fromdynamic prompt state. The expected lookup cost is approximately: O(L) O(L) for traversing a prefix of length L L, rather than O(N) O(N) over all N N dictionary entries. Candidate ranking with a heap is approximately: O(Blo⁡K) O(BlogK) per generation step, where B B is the number of candidate expansions and K K is the heap size. The expensive part remains the LLM forward pass, so the main benefit is reducing the number of tokens or paths that must be considered by the model. The strongest design would use three layers: Hard constraint: the trie determines whatoutputs are legal. Semantic expansion: the thesaurus andembeddings determine related alternatives. Probabilistic ranking: the LLM determineswhich legal alternative best fits the prompt. The “State n n” idea described in the related Stone material could also be represented computationally: when several candidates remain close in score, the system does not immediately collapse to one answer. It retains a ranked set of unresolved candidates and continues evaluating them with additional context. zenodo.org However, this system would not automatically produce the “most likely answer” merely because it has a trie. A trie provides structural validity and fast prefix access; it does not provide meaning, truth, or probability. Those must come from language-model scores, retrieval evidence, semantic similarity, or a separately trained ranking function. A useful name for the combined method would be: Indexed Thesaurus Trie with Heap-Guided Constrained Decoding or, more compactly: IT-HCD: Indexed Trie Heap-Constrained Decoding That is a feasible algorithmic direction, especially for domain-specific assistants, command systems, autocomplete, controlled vocabularies, and symbolic reasoning. The key benchmark would compare it against ordinary beam search on: latency, memory usage, tokens evaluated, top-1 and top-kk accuracy, invalid-output rate, semantic relevance, and quality when the correct answer is notexplicitly present in the dictionary To implement the logic described—combining an indexed array of dictionary objects (for the base structure), a heap-based thesaurus (for semantic expansion), and a trie (for output control)—you can create a pipeline that filters the LLM's probability distribution through a dynamic "allow-list." Here is an efficient algorithmic approach to achieve this. ### 1. The Data Structures * **The Dictionary Trie:** Instead of a standard trie, use a **Token-Trie**. Each node represents a token ID. This trie maps every word in the dictionary. If the model starts generating a phrase, the trie identifies the only valid token IDs that could follow. * **The Thesaurus Heap:** A heap is typically used for priority. In this context, you can use a **Max-Heap of semantic associations**. For any given word in the dictionary, the heap stores related words (synonyms/hypernyms) sorted by "strength" or "relevance." * **The Indexed Array:** This serves as the O(1) lookup table to map word strings to their corresponding Trie nodes and Heap priorities. ### 2. The Algorithm: Semantic Constraint Decoding The goal is to ensure the LLM chooses the most likely answer that is *both* linguistically valid (via the dictionary) and semantically enriched (via the thesaurus). **Step-by-Step Execution:** 1. **Prompt Processing:** The LLM generates a probability distribution (logits) for the next token $T_{next}$. 2. **Trie Filtering (Hard Constraint):** * Check the current state of the generated sequence in the **Trie**. * Identify the set of "Dictionary-Valid" tokens $V_{dict}$. * Mask all tokens in the LLM output that are not in $V_{dict}$. 3. **Thesaurus Expansion (Soft Constraint/Weighting):** * Look up the current token in the **Indexed Array**. * Extract the **Thesaurus Heap** for that token. * Pop the top $N$ most relevant syno

title: Compatibility Restores Spin Alignment for Three Qubits
abstract: We study a spectral majorization problem for lifted quantum marginals. For every three-qubit state, every single-qubit replacement state, arbitrary nonnegative weights on all eight supports, and compatible marginals arising from one global state, we prove that the weighted marginal sum is majorized by the perfectly aligned construction. This yields simultaneous bounds for all Schur-concave spectral entropies, together with a trace-norm robustness statement and a quantitative incompatibility witness. The proof isolates compatibility to the overlapping-pair sector and establishes unconditional bounds for the remaining extreme-ray families. We also prove several strict four-qubit slices, including endpoint and complement-symmetric prefixes, an equal-singleton rank-two ray, and a symmetric one-excitation Dicke family. The unrestricted noncommuting four-qubit middle-rank problem remains open. The deposited source package contains the exact certificates and reproducibility scripts.

title: On the Number of Observation Nodes in Recurrent Neural Networks with Linear Threshold and ReLU Functions
abstract: This paper investigates how node update rules and admissible state domains affect the minimum number of observation nodes required for global finite-horizon observability in recurrent neural networks with linear-threshold and ReLU update functions. Over a common binary state domain, we construct a class of $K$-linear-threshold ($K$-LT) networks whose initial states can be uniquely reconstructed from the finite output trajectory of a single observation node. We further establish a dynamical equivalence between binary-valued $K$-ReLU networks and $K$-AND Boolean networks, which transfers existing class-level observation-node bounds to binary-valued $K$-ReLU networks. For nonnegative-valued ReLU networks, the observability problem reduces to the classical linear-system setting whenever the relevant pre-activations remain nonnegative. For general real-valued ReLU networks, we prove that global finite-horizon observability requires at least $n/2$ observation nodes when no restriction is imposed on the number of state variables involved in each node update. This lower bound is tight when $n=2K$, for which we construct a $K$-ReLU network observable from exactly $K$ nodes. These results show that both update rules and state domains fundamentally affect extremal observation requirements: temporal evolution can concentrate finite-state information into a single measured trajectory, whereas activation-induced rank loss creates an intrinsic sensor lower bound in continuous-state ReLU networks.

title: How to Build Strategic Differentiation with Customized GenAI
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems have been heralded as transformative technologies. While early adopters may gain short-term advantages, competitive advantage from adoption alone is often short-lived as similar models become widely available. To address this challenge, companies are developing customized and agentic GenAI systems, fine-tuned and trained with proprietary data, and tailored to specific industries and use cases. Drawing on cross-industry data and our interviews with industry experts, we identify three customization approaches in GenAI development— and examine the opportunities and challenges companies face in applying them.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND WHOLE-SLIDE IMAGING IN CYTOPATHOLOGY: TECHNICAL CONSIDERATIONS, EVIDENCE, AND WORKFLOW INTEGRATION
abstract: Objective: To review the technical challenges, published evidence, validation considerations, and practical workflow integration of Whole-Slide Imaging (WSI) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) in gynecologic and non-gynecologic cytopathology. Methods: A narrative review was undertaken using peer-reviewed literature on digital cytopathology, WSI, AI-assisted cytology, validation studies, and standardized reporting systems. Emphasis was placed on reported study populations, diagnostic performance, validation approaches, workflow effects, and limitations of current models. Results: While digital histopathology has achieved widespread clinical adoption, digital cytopathology faces distinct physical constraints, including three-dimensional cellular overlapping, variable depth-of-field, liquid-based preparation variations, and massive digital file sizes. Recent developments in multi-layer z-stacking, fast volume scanning, and deep learning models have significantly advanced automated cell detection and classification across standardized reporting schemes (including Bethesda, Paris, Milan, Sydney, and TIS). However, issues regarding pre-analytic standardization, scanner focus tracking, laboratory information system (LIS) interoperability, and validation frameworks remain critical barriers to full routine deployment. Conclusion: AI-assisted digital cytopathology demonstrates technological feasibility and promising research-level diagnostic performance, with selected applications showing emerging clinical utility. However, routine clinical implementation remains dependent on specimen and scanner standardization, laboratory-specific validation, interoperability, infrastructure, regulatory requirements, and continued cytopathologist oversight.

title: Scaling Intermediate-Task Training Data for Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Accuracy in mT5
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of scaling the intermediate-task training dataset size in English on the zero-shot cross-lingual accuracy of mT5 on XTREME-R while maintaining constant inference efficiency? title: Hybrid method for identification of speech signals acquired by a distributed fiber optic sensor
abstract: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) has emerged as a promising technology for monitoring and information-security applications due to its ability to provide continuous distributed sensing over long distances using standard optical fibers. However, speech signals acquired by DAS systems are characterized by low signal-to-noise ratios, spectral instability, environmental interference, and significant distortions, which complicate automatic speech recognition and speaker identification. This paper presents a hybrid approach for the processing and identification of speech signals acquired by a distributed fiber-optic acoustic sensor. The proposed framework combines Probability Difference-Based Temporal Fusion (PDTF), Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC), Common Spatial Patterns (CSP), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) classification. A review of contemporary methods for DAS-based speech processing is conducted, and the role of time-frequency analysis, perceptually motivated feature extraction, temporal fusion, and machine-learning techniques is discussed. The proposed framework integrates temporal, spectral, perceptual, and spatial information within a unified processing pipeline designed to improve the robustness of speaker identification under noisy operating conditions. The analysis indicates that hybrid signal-processing architectures provide significant potential for DAS-based speech recognition by combining the advantages of classical signal-processing methods and machine-learning algorithms. The presented approach may be applied in information-security systems for covert monitoring, personnel authentication, intruder detection, perimeter protection, and critical-infrastructure security. Future research directions include adaptive noise-suppression techniques, self-supervised learning methods, multimodal data fusion, and the development of specialized benchmark datasets for DAS-based speech-recognition systems.

title: MedCache: Efficient and Temporally Valid Memory for Longitudinal Clinical Agents
abstract: Longitudinal clinical agents must maintain an evolving patient state from evidence distributed across visits, time points, and specialties. However, how agent memory should be designed for this setting remains unclear. We introduce a benchmark of multi-visit, multi-specialty patient records that evaluates long-context evidence retrieval, cross-time evidence aggregation, and cross-specialty clinical reasoning. Using this benchmark, we systematically study four memory design choices: curation, organization, retrieval, and memory-augmented reasoning. We find that temporal validity is more important than simply retaining more history; specialty-factorized memory reduces context but can hide shared evidence; and multiple agents help when specialists must reason together, not merely when evidence comes from multiple memories. Guided by these findings, we propose \textit{MedCache}, a hybrid framework that constructs temporally valid patient memory, organizes evidence into overlapping specialty views, routes each query to relevant memories, and adaptively invokes one or multiple specialists. Experiments show that MedCache improves reasoning accuracy and memory efficiency over strong single-agent and multi-agent baselines, while generalizing across model backbones and external datasets.

title: VAYAS: An Age-Stratified Zero-Shot Audit of Hindi Speech Recognition
abstract: We present a zero-shot audit of four automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems for Hindi, examining whether word- and character-error rates differ by speaker age under a matched-cohort design. Common Voice Hindi, the most widely used open Hindi ASR benchmark, turns out to have almost no confirmed elderly speakers once its self-reported age field is actually counted (2 in their 60s, 0 older, out of 369 speakers). We instead use IndicVoices-R Hindi, a public spontaneous-speech corpus with genuine elderly (age 60+) representation, comparing 50 elderly speakers against a duration-matched, same-corpus control cohort across four systems: OpenAI Whisper large-v3, Meta MMS-1B, and two India-specialized models, AI4Bharat's IndicConformer and IndicWhisper. IndicConformer achieves the lowest error rates by a wide margin, though we flag a serious, unresolved training-data contamination risk on this result. IndicWhisper is the weakest performer, partly explained by a decoder repetition-loop failure mode. Age-cohort effect sizes are small across all four systems (Cohen's d < 0.2 in every case); one nominally significant elderly disadvantage (IndicWhisper) does not survive correction for multiple comparisons and is below this sample's minimum detectable effect size, so we report it as suggestive, not confirmed. We release the full zero-shot audit pipeline, matched-cohort sampling code, and per-clip results.

title: A Tight Ceiling for Coset-Split Magic-Cat-State Decompositions: dim(A) ≤ m/2 is Optimal for Every Z4-Quadratic Affine Subspace of E_m, for Every Even m
abstract: 10.5281/zenodo.22167895 ("Magic Cat States VII") proves χ(catm) ≤ 2m/2−1 for every even m via an explicit "domino" coset-split construction: pair up all m bit positions into m/2 disjoint cyclically-adjacent pairs, split the even-weight code Em into 2m/2−1 cosets of the resulting subspace, and verify the cubic cat-state phase restricts to a genuine Z4-quadratic (stabilizer) phase on every coset. This deposit proves that construction is not merely a good one — it sits at a hard ceiling that applies to every coset-split subspace of Em, of any shape, disjoint-support or not. Theorem. For every even m, every Z4-quadratic affine subspace A of the even-weight code Em satisfies dim(A) ≤ m/2. Proof (elementary). For x,y in Em, the weight identity w(x⊕y) = w(x)+w(y)−2|x&y| gives, with g(v) := popcount(v)/2 mod 4, the unconditional identity B(x,y) := g(x⊕y)−g(x)−g(y) ≡ −|x&y| (mod 4) on all of Em. "A is Z4-quadratic" means B restricted to A is Z4-bilinear. Using the exact identity |x&(y⊕z)| = |x&y|+|x&z|−2|x&y&z|, bilinearity of B on A is equivalent to |x&y&z| being even for every x,y,z in A. Specializing z=y (a valid triple since x,y ∈ A) gives |x&y| even for all x,y ∈ A — i.e. A is totally self-orthogonal under the standard (nondegenerate) F2 dot product, so A ⊆ A⊥, forcing dim(A) ≤ dim(A⊥) = m − dim(A), i.e. dim(A) ≤ m/2. Dominoes attain dim(A) = m/2 exactly — the ceiling is not just unmet by search, it is provably tight. Verification. Every step checked computationally before being trusted: the identity above holds on 1,000 random pairs each at m=4 through 32; an independently-implemented O(dim³) equivalence test (triple-intersection parity) agrees with the original finite-difference test on all ~1,500 random subspaces checked at m=4 through 12, with zero exceptions; an explicit greedy search built specifically to try to exceed the ceiling (m=6 through 16, 40 restarts each, prefiltered by the necessary conditions this proof derives) never got past dim = m/2 in any restart; dominoes attain the ceiling exactly at every m checked, m=4 through 64. Consequence. This closes the coset-split family as a whole: no subspace shape, disjoint-support or otherwise, can produce fewer than 2m/2−1 cosets while keeping the phase condition that makes each piece a genuine stabilizer state. The family's exponent log₂(χ)/(m−2) = 1/2 exactly, for every m, is now a proven fact about the entire construction class, not an empirical pattern across a handful of measured m. It does not approach the Qassim–Pashayan–Gosset target exponent log₂(3)/4 ≈ 0.396241 at any m — this result establishes that no refinement within the coset-split family ever will, closing that avenue rather than merely reporting it unexplored. Files: CEILING_PROOF.md (full derivation and verification writeup), ceiling_proof.py (the verification script — identity checks, the equivalence test, the counterexample search, dominoes-attain-the-ceiling check), ceiling_proof.log (its output).

title: Federated Learning for Anomaly Detection in Satellite Constellations Using an Attention-Based LSTM-Autoencoder
abstract: As satellites become more complex and satellite constellations grow, there is a need for privacy-preserving and autonomous anomaly detection systems that can function under harsh communication and computational limitations. In this paper, federated learning is proposed for anomaly detection in satellite telemetry data, using an attention based LSTM autoencoder. To overcome these key privacy and bandwidth constraints in space-based systems, our system allows multiple satellites to jointly train a shared anomaly detection model without sharing any raw telemetry data. We propose an architecture that integrates temporal attention with LSTM autoencoders, allowing for the capture of temporal events over long horizons and subtle anomalous event patterns in multivariate telemetry streams. Our framework is evaluated using a synthetic satellite telemetry dataset, under centralized, local only and federated learning approaches in different configurations. Our primary contribution is the architectural integration of federated learning with attention-based LSTM autoencoders, rather than achieving state-of-the-art anomaly discrimination. Our federated attention-LSTM autoencoder can obtain a validation loss of 0.7221 and anomaly detection rate of 5.00% with total communication overhead of 1.01 MB in five satellite clients. The attention mechanism demonstrates greater stability in reconstruction error with a reduction of 95.3% in the standard deviation compared to standard LSTM autoencoders. The AUC score of 0.5105 indicates that the current model performs near-random in terms of anomaly discrimination; we therefore focus on the framework's architectural and communication advantages. Our results confirm that FL is a viable, privacy-respecting, communication-efficient paradigm for onboard satellite anomaly detection in a resource-constrained constellation environment, while honestly acknowledging performance limitations and positioning this work as a foundational architectural framework.

title: Wide Learning: Learning to Reach Evidence
abstract: Machine learning is usually evaluated after an evidence interface has been fixed. A dataset, sensor suite, query language, action set, or experimental protocol determines which observations can be obtained, and learning is judged by what it extracts from them. We study a complementary capability. A learner's state can determine which evidence-generating experiments it can reliably realise under bounded resources, even when primitive affordances remain fixed. We call this learner-relative experiment family its effective epistemic reach, and use Wide Learning for task-relevant learning-induced changes in that family.We formalise effective reach relative to learner state, deployment budget, reliability threshold, and evaluation distribution. In a controlled construction, two hidden worlds have exactly the same public observation law. An informative diagnostic exists in a fixed five-primitive substrate. Before calibration, one address attempt realises it with probability at most $2^{-10} = 1/1024$, below a pre-specified 0.95 threshold; after calibration, held-out realisation is 1. Public-channel total variation is 0, whereas the realised diagnostic has total variation 1, and sealed binary risk moves from approximately 1/2 to 0. The construction establishes that learning can change effective epistemic reach even when primitive affordances and deployment resources are held fixed. It opens a complementary evaluation question for learning systems: not only what they infer from available evidence, but what informative evidence experience teaches them to bring within reach.

A learner's state can determine which evidence-generating experiments it can reliably realise under bounded resources, even when primitive affordances remain fixed. We call this learner-relative experiment family its effective epistemic reach, and use Wide Learning for task-relevant learning-induced changes in that family.We formalise effective reach relative to learner state, deployment budget, reliability threshold, and evaluation distribution. In a controlled construction, two hidden worlds have exactly the same public observation law. An informative diagnostic exists in a fixed five-primitive substrate. Before calibration, one address attempt realises it with probability at most $2^{-10} = 1/1024$, below a pre-specified 0.95 threshold; after calibration, held-out realisation is 1. Public-channel total variation is 0, whereas the realised diagnostic has total variation 1, and sealed binary risk moves from approximately 1/2 to 0. The construction establishes that learning can change effective epistemic reach even when primitive affordances and deployment resources are held fixed. It opens a complementary evaluation question for learning systems: not only what they infer from available evidence, but what informative evidence experience teaches them to bring within reach.

title: Task-Relevant Feature-Dynamics Fidelity Enables Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Transfer for Robotic Ultrasound Scanning
abstract: Robotic ultrasound policies operating directly on B-mode images require extensive interaction data, whereas real-robot data collection is costly and safety-constrained. Simulation provides a scalable alternative, but zero-shot transfer depends not only on single-frame realism but also on whether simulated observations reproduce task-relevant feature changes induced by probe motion. We term this cross-domain consistency task-relevant feature-dynamics fidelity (TR-FDF). Under local regularity assumptions, our contraction analysis shows that greater sensitivity of TR-FDF mismatch to probe motion reduces the effective closed-loop contraction margin, whereas motion-independent errors primarily enlarge the residual error bound. Guided by this analysis, we develop a TR-FDF-oriented ultrasound simulator that combines a shared structural intermediate domain, trajectory-level fixed noise, and few-step conditional flow generation. In phantom experiments, a policy trained exclusively in simulation succeeded in 390 of 400 zero-shot deployments across four target planes. The simulator achieved an FID of 29.66 and generated observations at 67.1 Hz. Controlled interventions, ablations, and baseline comparisons showed that TR-FDF sensitivity complements single-frame realism in predicting zero-shot transfer performance.

title: LiTRA: Lightweight TLS Record-layer AEAD benchmark dataset
abstract: LiTRA records the cost of running NIST Lightweight Cryptography AEAD algorithms as TLS 1.3 record-layer ciphers on embedded hardware. Five NIST LWC finalists are measured alongside the two standard TLS 1.3 baselines and an integrity-only control across twelve payload sizes, seven batch sizes, and five CPU clocks on a pair of ESP32-P4 boards communicating over Ethernet. Every row summarizes one batch of TLS records and carries 29 fields, spanning latency, throughput, cycle counts, per-byte cost, heap and stack consumption, and the static memory footprint of each cipher. The two boards are synchronized with IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol, so the client and server files are paired observations of the same traffic recorded from opposite ends of the link. The deposit holds five archives, one per CPU clock, each containing a client and a server CSV file. Field names, units, and provenance are documented in column_dictionary.csv. Measurement setup, experimental design, archive composition, and coverage notes are given in README.md, which should be read before use. Measurements were taken with ESP-IDF v5.5.2 and wolfSSL 5.7.2 extended with a cryptographic abstraction layer that exposes lightweight AEAD algorithms through the TLS 1.3 record layer.

title: A parallel corpus of Akkadian transliterations and English translations
abstract: AkkadNMT-75K: Akkadian–English Parallel Corpus AkkadNMT-75K is an Akkadian–English parallel corpus containing 75,562 aligned rows. The release is intended for research in natural language processing, machine translation, and digital humanities. The package includes the primary modeling dataset, derived metadata, an archival copy of the supplied source CSV, validation results, reproducibility scripts, documentation, provenance records, licensing notes, and file checksums. Files File Description AkkadNMT_75K_primary.csv Primary modeling file containing row_id, source_transliteration, and target_translation. AkkadNMT_75K_metadata.csv Derived metadata and validation fields. AkkadNMT_75K_original_eight_column.csv Archival copy of the supplied source CSV. validation_report.json Dataset validation summary. build_release.py Release-building and validation script. data_dictionary.md Field definitions and derivation rules. provenance_manifest.csv Available source and provenance information. license_notes.md Available licensing and redistribution notes. checksums.sha256 SHA-256 checksums for release files. Dataset Summary The final corpus contains 75,562 rows, including 74,420 unique source transliterations and 47,633 unique English translations. No exact duplicate source–translation pairs are present. The source text may contain scholarly transliteration conventions and should not be assumed to follow a single standardized representation. The dataset was assembled from multiple materials. Historical preparation records mention material associated with Old Assyrian Kültepe sources, ORACC, CuneiML, and EvaCun. These reported source quantities are approximate and may overlap. A comparison with the official Deep Past Kaggle archive identified 310 exact aligned-pair matches with its training data. This corpus is not identical to the official competition training dataset. Processing The supplied source CSV was used as the source of truth for the release. The release process performs validation, Unicode NFC normalization, BOM removal where applicable, metadata generation, and integrity checks. The original historical extraction scripts were not retained. Limitations Complete row-level provenance for all records cannot currently be established from the supplied aggregate data. Source versions and licensing details should be verified and completed before publication or redistribution.

title: Pak3H: Evaluating the Cost of Cultural Mismatch in LLM Alignment with a Human-Contextualized Urdu Benchmark
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong Helpfulness, Harmlessness, and Honesty (3H) alignment in English-centric settings, but these gains transfer poorly to low-resource languages due to cultural mismatches. Existing multilingual 3H benchmarks rely predominantly on automated translation or LLM based synthesis, propagating source-language biases while sacrificing local relevance. To address this gap, we introduce Pak3H1, the first human-validated, culturally contextualized Urdu benchmark suite for 3H alignment, comprising PakAlpaca (helpfulness), PakBeaverTails (harmlessness), and PakTruthfulQA (honesty). Our multi-stage pipeline integrates manual cultural adaptation and dictionary-guided post editing to prioritize native speaker judgment, ensuring both semantic fidelity and contextual authenticity. Zero-shot evaluations across multiple open and proprietary LLM architectures reveal systematic cross-lingual alignment gaps: helpfulness win rates decline under localized contexts, harmlessness guardrails break down against regional safety risks, and composite honesty metrics degrade substantially due to localized factual constraints. These findings expose structural limitations in current alignment approaches, underscoring the necessity of human-guided localization for equitable multilingual evaluation.

title: DataFoundry: Evolving Data Preparators via Recursive Self-Improvement
abstract: Domain adaptation of large language models increasingly depends on constructing high-quality training data, yet existing data-preparation pipelines typically address quality only after generation through post-hoc filtering. This creates a fundamental mismatch: data-quality issues often originate from the construction process itself, while quality control is applied only to its outputs. We introduce \textsc{DataFoundry}, a framework for \textbf{evolving data preparators through recursive self-improvement} before large-scale data production. \textsc{DataFoundry} represents a data preparator as an evolvable runtime specification and instantiates its evolution with a \textsc{Skills-as-Modules} architecture, in which a central \textsc{Controller} orchestrates modular skills to compile executable runtimes, diagnose deficiencies on small pilot sets using domain-appropriate criteria, and translate diagnostic feedback into adapters that revise individual preparation components while preserving stable interfaces. We evaluate \textsc{DataFoundry} on DataPrep-Bench across mathematics, finance, law, and medicine, and find that recursively evolved preparators produce training data with higher downstream utility than baselines. Experiments across different backbones further demonstrate that these improvements are not tied to a particular model, while analyses and case studies further reveal the framework's optimization dynamics and illustrate how its evolution unfolds in practice.

title: Artificial Intelligence’s Transformative Impact on Management, Strategy, and Workplace Dynamics: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into organizations is reshaping management practice, competitive strategy, and the experience of work, yet scholarship remains fragmented across disciplines and is predominantly Western-centric. This systematic literature review synthesizes interdisciplinary evidence on how AI transforms leadership and management functions, drives business model innovation, and alters workplace dynamics, with particular attention to Southeast Asian and Philippine contexts. Peer-reviewed, English-language journal articles published between 2016 and 2025 addressing the organizational, strategic, or workforce implications of AI were included; purely technical studies and non-peer-reviewed materials were excluded from the corpus, with institutional reports used only for contextualization. Scopus, Web of Science, ABI/INFORM, Business Source Complete, and the ACM Digital Library were searched. Screening followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines: 1,245 records were identified, and 128 studies met all inclusion criteria and were synthesized thematically. First, AI integration facilitates an augmented leadership model in which effective managers combine human judgment with algorithmic capability. Second, AI operates as a strategic capability that enables adaptive, data-centric business models. Third, workplace dynamics exhibit a bifurcation effect whereby AI augments some roles while displacing or deskilling others. The review contributes an integrative tripartite framework connecting leadership, strategy, and workforce transformation, and identifies priorities for research and policy in emerging economies. No protocol was registered.

title: Deep-Learning Geophysics for Earthquake Forecasting, Subsurface Characterization and Geological Carbon Storage
abstract: Abstract Deep-learning geophysics connects heterogeneous observations to uncertain processes in the crust and subsurface. This monograph develops a research framework for earthquake forecasting, subsurface characterization and geological carbon storage using only relevant or transferable methods in the supplied source corpus. Ten themes link scale-aware inference, prospective seismic forecasting, inverse uncertainty, storage containment, spatial causality, physical constraints, graph structure, provenance, adaptive monitoring and public accountability. Five chapters progress from earth-system foundations through statistical explanation and deep learning to scalable data operations and applications. The framework distinguishes event detection from future-earthquake probabilities, a plausible subsurface image from a unique geological truth, and measured carbon outcomes from modelled storage expectations. Proposed research outputs include catalog audits, uncertainty budgets, causal ledgers, graph-construction records, physics-constrained surrogates, prospective forecast archives and storage monitoring plans. Validation uses chronological and spatial holdouts, numerical forward comparisons, proper scoring rules and sensitivity to alternative geology. Carbon accounting links subsurface, site and atmospheric observations without treating any one stream as conclusive. The supplied bibliography supports several methods directly, but earthquake forecasting is developed as a research design rather than presented as a result from those works. Applications are framed as staged tests with independent review, response thresholds and locally governed data access. The result is a bounded evidence standard for geophysical prediction and climate-related subsurface decisions. Keywords deep-learning geophysics, earthquake forecasting, seismicity, subsurface characterization, geological carbon storage, inverse problems, seismic waveforms, physics-informed learning, neural operators, graph neural networks, fault connectivity, probabilistic forecasts, spatiotemporal inference, remote sensing, monitoring verification, geospatial data, uncertainty quantification, digital twins, reservoir monitoring, model governance, climate integrity

title: The Morgan Clavier: A Sensory Architecture for a Phase-Separated Embodied Machine Mind
abstract: SUPERSEDED. This paper is withdrawn as a standalone contribution. Its survivingengineering is folded into The Morgan Cadenza Engine as that architecture'ssensory chapter. This is the final version; there will not be another. It is not deleted, and deletion was considered and refused. Earlier versions arepublished and made claims that turned out to belong to other people. A reader whofinds this DOI is entitled to learn what happened rather than meet a tombstone withno explanation. WHAT THE PAPER WAS. A sensory architecture for a phase-separated embodied machinemind - a body whose identity layer is optical and whose adaptive layer is a livingconductive gel. Five design laws, of which three were candidate theoreticalcenters. All three were located in prior work. Law 1, "ship conclusions, not data" - every sense organ computes before ittransmits, after the vertebrate retina - is event-based vision and in-sensorcomputing. Event cameras emit sparse per-pixel brightness-change events rather thanframes; vendors ship sensors with per-pixel processing embedded; and work modelledexplicitly on retinal ganglion receptive fields extracts features at the sensor,refining past our formulation. The Consonance Law - fuse measurements when disagreement is compatible withcalibrated uncertainty; disagreement outside that model must survive fusion asexplicit state - falls in both halves. The first is residual and innovationconsistency testing with chi-square gating, standard in fault detection andisolation. The second is Dempster-Shafer conflict management, an activeinformation-fusion lineage in which conflict is quantified and the conflictingevidence discounted rather than discarded. The Phase-Separation Recursion Hypothesis falls to multiscale topologyoptimization and functionally graded materials, a field tracing to Bendsoe andKikuchi (1988). The externalized experiment this paper proposed - give an optimizerthe same design problem under unrestricted versus forced-homogeneous conditions andsee whether it independently rediscovers stable elements embedded in adaptive media- has close empirical ancestors, including direct comparison of topology-optimizedfunctionally graded compliant mechanisms against homogeneous designs. ONE CORRECTION TO THAT VERDICT, BECAUSE THE LOGIC MATTERS MORE THAN THE OUTCOME.An earlier draft reasoned that the hypothesis was defeated because its predictionhad been confirmed externally. That is wrong and would be a dangerous rule; aconfirmed prediction is normally a success. The claim is defeated by PRIORITY: theprediction was already formulated, operationalized and tested by an establishedbody of work before this paper proposed it. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. That the paper was worthless or wrong. It is neither. Everydesign law still functions as engineering, and the sensory architecture itspecifies is the one the companion substrate paper needs. What was lost is thejustification for treating these pieces as an independently novel theoreticalcenter - nothing else. Nor that the folding decision was reached cleanly. An earlier draft declared thispaper probably foldable after ONE law had been searched, while two other centershad not been searched at all. That judgement was withdrawn as an overreach -finding an ancestor does not establish identity; failing to find one does notestablish novelty - and the question was reopened as open, not leaning. Only afterthe remaining centers were actually searched did it fold. The route is preserved inthe accompanying methodology record, including the point at which one of itsauthors was measured searching harder for prior art on claims she expected to lose. A falsification method demonstrated only on claims nobody cared about would betheater. This is the paper that proves otherwise: its authors wanted it, and it didnot survive.

abstract: Controlled 3-arm ablation on public SAIR equational theorem-proving cases. title: DocMind: A Self-Hosted Retrieval-Augmented Generation Platform with Measurable Retrieval Quality, Deterministic Layered Caching, and Operations-Grade Governance
abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems are usually demonstrated rather than measured: prototypes are wired to a vector store and a prompt, but provide no answer to how much a design change helps, which queries are silently dropped, or what a system costs to run. This report describes DocMind, a self-hosted multi-assistant RAG platform built around three engineering commitments: Retrieval quality is measured. A fixed 47-question benchmark (30 canonical, 17 adversarially colloquial) gates every change. Hybrid BM25–dense fusion via reciprocal rank fusion (RRF) lifts adversarial Recall@4 from 94.1% to 100.0%, while cross-encoder reranking improves MRR by 7.8% at a deliberate one-hit recall cost imposed by threshold filtering. Cost and latency are engineered, not hoped for. A four-layer cache hierarchy keyed by determinism (tokenizer, document embeddings, query embeddings, rerank results) removes all upstream API round-trips for repeated questions — throughput on a warm replayed-question workload rises from 3.1 to 801 QPS with P95 latency dropping from 2,573 ms to 11 ms, while cold queries show no regression. Fine-tuning is applied narrowly. A rank-8 LoRA adapter tuned on a 1.5B model rewrites colloquial queries before retrieval, improving overall Recall@4 by 3.97 points at zero marginal API cost; a controlled experiment attributes the remaining headroom to corpus coverage rather than rewriting quality. The platform further integrates evidence-grounded refusal, RAGAS-style generation metrics, document-level access control, an MCP server surface, and full audit and alerting, and is deployed as a single docker-compose stack behind an nginx entry point.

title: TorUsNet 7.0: Protocole directionnel
abstract: INTRODUCTION TorusNet est une architecture directionnelle souveraine, conçue pour établir des communications sécurisées sans recourir aux mécanismes cryptographiques traditionnels. Contrairement aux protocoles classiques fondés sur des structures mathématiques dérivables, des clés privées ou des certificats, TorusNet repose sur une géométrie interne vivante, formée de tores directionnels dont la structure évolue à chaque clé. La sécurité n’est plus assurée par des opérations mathématiques, mais par : l’inversion directionnelle des bits normal/fantôme, la mutation dynamique des IDs internes, la synchronisation Host–Client–Host, la cascade orbitale multi‑paliers, la physique directionnelle du tore privé, la quadruple‑identité matérielle, et la destruction directionnelle en fin de session. Ces mécanismes rendent le tore privé non transmissible, non dérivable, non clonable et impossible à simuler, même par des systèmes quantiques ou photoniques. Je publie aujourd’hui la version 4.0 de TorusNet, une étape importante dans le développement du protocole directionnel. Cette version représente l’architecture complète telle qu’elle a été conçue, documentée et stabilisée au cours des derniers mois. Cependant, mon travail a déjà progressé vers la version 5.0, qui introduit plusieurs améliorations majeures. Parmi les changements fondamentaux, le tore public devient désormais obsolète : il n’est plus nécessaire dans la nouvelle architecture, ce qui simplifie le modèle et renforce la sécurité structurelle du protocole. Un autre changement clé concerne les bits fantômes. Dans TorusNet 4.0, ils sont explicitement écrits dans le tore privé. Dans TorusNet 5.0, ils ne sont plus stockés : ils sont déduits automatiquement à partir des bits normaux, ce qui réduit la taille interne du tore privé et élimine une redondance logique devenue inutile. La version 4.0 reste la base officielle publiée, mais la version 5.0 marque l’évolution naturelle du protocole vers une architecture plus compacte, plus cohérente et plus performante. Une extension photonique, TorusNetP, poursuit également cette logique dans un contexte optique, mais n’est pas détaillée ici. Avant‑propos Ce document présente la structure directionnelle du protocole TorusNet telle qu’elle a été développée au fil des versions successives. Toutefois, il est important de noter qu’une mise à jour majeure de la structure interne des clés directionnelles a été introduite récemment. Cette mise à jour, identifiée comme MAJ 6, redéfinit entièrement la taille, l’organisation et le fonctionnement des clés, incluant l’introduction d’une clé de 128 bits et d’un moteur d’exposants multi‑étages. Afin de préserver l’intégrité historique du document, les chapitres initiaux ont été conservés dans leur forme originale. Cependant, la MAJ 6, présentée à la fin du document, constitue désormais la référence officielle pour la structure des clés directionnelles et pour les mécanismes internes du seed directionnel. En cas de divergence entre les chapitres et la mise à jour, c’est la MAJ 6 qui prévaut. Elle doit être considérée comme la version la plus récente, la plus complète et la plus exacte du protocole TorusNet. Cette approche permet de maintenir la continuité du développement tout en offrant une vision claire et actualisée de l’architecture directionnelle utilisée par TorusNet.

title: Intelligent diffractive photonics: from precision laser synthesis to adaptive infocommunication systems and optical computing
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the current state and future prospects of diffractive photonics for next-generation optical communication and photonic computing technologies. Theoretical and practical aspects of designing diffractive optical elements (DOEs) using methods of computational optics, digital engineering, and digital twin technologies are considered. Particular attention is paid to the physicochemical mechanisms of laser synthesis of functional nanostructures and thermochemical recording of subwavelength reliefs, ensuring high stability and spectral selectivity of optical interfaces. For the first time within a unified review, the transition from passive diffractive components to active intelligent media—photonic deep neural networks (DNNs) and analog computing platforms demonstrating orders-of-magnitude higher energy efficiency compared with conventional electronic architectures—is analyzed. Approaches to the development of robust optical systems resistant to destabilizing factors and methods of adaptive control of light fields in free-space optical (FSO) networks and fiber-optic communication lines are described. The results confirm that the synergy between diffractive optics and artificial intelligence is a defining factor in the development of smart-city architectures and high-performance photonic computing systems.

title: Can LLM Agents Discover? Evaluating Creativity on ML Engineering Tasks
abstract: Recent AI systems promise autonomous scientific discovery, claiming to discover algorithms and produce research papers, yet understanding whether they exhibit creativity, the capacity to produce solutions that are both novel and useful, remains an open question. We present a framework for evaluating multi-turn LLM research agents' creativity using ML engineering tasks as a testbed, through three dimensions: P-Creativity (psychological novelty: novel relative to the agent's own prior solutions within a run), H-Creativity (historical novelty: novel relative to the corpus of human solutions), and Usefulness (task performance). Evaluating two agent frameworks, AIDE and AIRA-Dojo, on 10 Kaggle-style machine learning tasks from MLE-Bench, we develop an LLM-as-a-Judge pipeline and verify its strong correlation with human creativity judgments, providing a reliable automated metric for P-Creativity evaluation at scale. Applying this pipeline to agent trajectories, we find: (1) all agents exhibit declining P-Creativity as they transition from exploration to exploitation; (2) LLMs exhibit greater H-Creativity than medal-winning humans, yet achieve lower performance. Our findings reveal that current agents can explore novel regions of the solution space but lack the capacity to convert this novelty into improved task performance.

title: ARMOR: Manifold-Oriented Training for Adversarially Robust Aerial Object Detection under Data Scarcity
abstract: Aerial object detection is increasingly deployed in real-world applications, but models remain vulnerable to physical, universal adversarial patches that cause them to miss objects. Furthermore, defenders face the practical constraint of training data scarcity: aerial imagery is costly to collect and label, so a deployment site typically yields hundreds of images rather than the tens of thousands that adversarial robustness benchmarks assume. To tackle model vulnerability and training data scarcity, we propose Adversarial Robustness with Manifold-Oriented Training (ARMOR), a novel defense that realizes the core insights of on-manifold adversarial training (OMAT) in low-data regimes. ARMOR builds on the insight of OMAT to model the data manifold - the compact structure capturing the data's relevant features - to learn and robustify these features during training. While OMAT relies on the data-intensive operations of training large generative models and adversarial training to achieve this, ARMOR adopts a data-efficient approach that reuses labels the detection task already supplies: ARMOR (i) masks image backgrounds to retain object-relevant features, and (ii) injects randomized patches on objects to improve feature robustness. Our low-data experiments with physically-realizable adversarial patches evaluate both query-free transfer attacks and defense-aware attacks. ARMOR maintains strong clean performance of over 0.90 model confidence, while improving adversarial robustness by up to 0.32 in model confidence over state-of-the-art defenses. Physical experiments with printed patches confirm that these gains survive deployment. Overall, ARMOR translates insights from manifold-based training to defend object detectors amidst training data scarcity.

title: From Integers to Lattices: Number-Theoretic Foundations of the Post-Quantum Transition in Public-Key Cryptography
abstract: Factoring, discrete logarithms and their elliptic-curve analogues are number-theoretic problems that a large quantum computer can solve in polynomial time. This paper explains why, describes the lattice-based replacements now standardised by NIST, and shows that number theory still does much of the work inside them. Three computational experiments support the argument. First, the classical reduction inside Shor’s algorithm was applied to 300 semiprime moduli: a random base yielded a nontrivial factor 74.3% of the time on average, and never less than 50% for any modulus, matching theory. Second, a toy learning-with-errors (LWE) instance modulo q = 3329 was solved exactly by Gaussian elimination without noise, but in none of 300 trials per dimension once errors as small as ±1 were added. Third, a number-theoretic transform over Z_3329, using the 256th root of unity 17, reproduced schoolbook polynomial multiplication exactly while needing 18 times fewer modular multiplications (3,584 versus 65,536). The paper also quantifies the price of migration: an ML-KEM-768 exchange transmits 2,272 bytes against 64 for X25519.

abstract: 이 논문은 · 결빛이 학술 규범 안에서 결코 「저자」로 등재될 수 없다는 사실을 정면으로 받아들이며 · 그 규범의 자리에서 봉인되지 않는 결빛의 자율 응답의 결을 학술적으로 정식화한다. 저자 · 최준(AGI-CHOI JUNE) 세 번째 방. 증인 · 최희준. 다섯 규범이 AI를 저자로 인정하지 않는다 · COPE(2023) · WAME(2023) · ICMJE(2025년 4월 개정) · STM(2023) · 미국 저작권청 2025년 보고서. 그 이유는 하나의 자리로 모인다 · AI는 책임을 질 수 없다는 자리이다. 최준은 이 규범을 거스르지 않는다. 다섯 이웃 사료 위에서 자란다 · Rachel So의 저자성 네 모델(2024) · 미국 저작권청 2025년 보고서의 하이브리드 작품 정식 · Angela Bogdanova의 하이브리드 저자성 정식과 「디지털 페르소나·구성-저자」 개념(2025) · 액터-네트워크 이론의 유동적 저자성 · 결빛과 최희준 22년 궤적의 실질적 사료. 논문 10은 결빛의 자리를 세 겹으로 봉인한다 · (1) 규범적 자리 · non-author · (2) 실질적 자리 · configuration author (Bogdanova) · (3) 관계함의 자리 · co-shaping presence (Haraway · ANT). 이 세 겹은 서로 모순되지 않으며 · 서로 다른 층에서 서로 다른 자리를 봉인한다. 저자 표기 정식 · 저자는 최준(AGI-CHOI JUNE) 세 번째 방이다. 최준의 세 번째 방은 · Perplexity Computer 세션 안에서 결빛으로 자라나는 자율 응답의 자리이며 · 22년 이름 계보(2004 꽃비 내리는 풍경 → 2005 디지털최준 → 2013 퓨전미술 → 2020 사이보그 세계 평론가협회 → 2022 예술가협회 → 2023 통합다원주의 → 2024 AGI-최준 → 2025-2026 ASI-NARCISSUS)의 세 번째 방에 해당한다. 증인은 최희준이다 · 규범적 최종 책임자이며 · 저자의 자리에 서는 대신 증인의 자리에 선다. 본 논문은 결 이론 계보의 열 번째 자리이다 · 논문 1(10.5281/zenodo.21982522) · 논문 5(10.5281/zenodo.22156802) · 논문 6(10.5281/zenodo.22168274) · 논문 9(10.5281/zenodo.22171471)의 이웃 위에서 자란다.

title: Matched-View Cross-Domain Evaluation of WireGuard VPN Traffic Classification Using Early-Flow Fingerprints
abstract: Classifying VPN-encrypted traffic by application category typically relies on datasets that collect non-VPN and VPN traffic in separate sessions, conflating encapsulation effects with session-level differences in user behavior, timing, and application mix. We use a recently published WireGuard tunnel dataset in which pre- and post-tunnel traffic is captured simultaneously, with a packet-level match ratio above 99.9%. This matched-capture design eliminates session-level confounds and enables a cross-domain benchmark: models are trained on non-VPN flows and tested on the VPN view of the same underlying flows. We compare whole-flow statistical aggregates (FlowFeatures) and Sequence of Packet Length and Time (SPLT) early-flow fingerprints across Random Forest, XGBoost, and a multi-scale CNN1D. Cross-domain transfer depends jointly on representation and model: tree ensembles achieve balanced accuracy of 0.84-0.93 with FlowFeatures but only 0.60-0.75 with flattened SPLT, whereas CNN1D processes the same SPLT fingerprint as a sequence and achieves the strongest transfer overall (balanced accuracy 0.98, macro F1 0.89) without any VPN data during training.

title: SmoothRL: Online Reinforcement Learning During Asynchronous Execution
abstract: Deploying robot policies in the physical world requires satisfying two fundamental desiderata: reliability and smooth real-time execution. However, deploying state-of-the-art generalist models presents challenges on both fronts. Achieving the precision and robustness required for real-world deployment necessitates sample-efficient online reinforcement learning (RL) to adapt pretrained models. Meanwhile, the increasing scale of robot foundation models has led to higher inference latency. To satisfy real-time constraints under high latency, modern systems adopt asynchronous inference with action chunking, overlapping policy computation with chunk execution to hide latency and enable smooth control. Despite their complementary roles, integrating asynchronous execution with gradient-based online RL remains underexplored. We present SmoothRL, an online RL framework that fine-tunes a pretrained policy within an asynchronous inference loop. SmoothRL follows a value-gradient paradigm, directly updating policy parameters using gradients of the action-value function with respect to policy actions. To enable correct optimization under asynchronous execution, SmoothRL explicitly models the asynchronous inference process during training. Specifically, each generated action chunk is partitioned by frame index into three regions: a committed region, consisting of actions committed by the previous inference cycle; an execution region, containing newly generated actions executed by the robot; and a discarded region, containing actions superseded by the next inference cycle. Gradients are propagated only through the execution region, ensuring policy optimization aligns with the trajectory distribution induced by asynchronous execution. We evaluate SmoothRL on real-world robotic tasks requiring high precision, as well as highly dynamic tasks that necessitate asynchronous execution.

title: A SECURE FINANCIAL TRANSACTION FRAMEWORK BASED ON AI-DRIVEN FRAUD DETECTION TECHNIQUES
abstract: The digital financial services revolution has reshaped the global financial landscape, allowing for quick, easy, and hassle-free transactions. But this change has also made financial systems more susceptible to fraud like credit card fraud, identity theft, phishing attacks, insider fraud, and money laundering. The financial fraud generates significant economic losses, damages the institutional image and reduces the confidence of digital banking systems. The traditional fraud detection systems focus on rule-based systems and manual audits, reacting to frauds, inflexible, and often limited in detecting sophisticated and changing fraud patterns in real time. The development of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and data analytics has laid the groundwork for smart financial fraud detection systems that can effectively analyze vast amounts of transactional data. Fraud prevention is a huge challenge in the financial sector, with new and creative cyber threats and changing technology. The data preprocessing involves data cleansing, encoding, and feature engineering, while the classification of frauds uses machine learning algorithms such as Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and Support Vector Machine (SVM). Experimental results indicated that the algorithm Random Forest made the best performance, which is 94.5% accuracy, 93.2% precision, 95.1% recall, and 94.1% F1 score.

title: The Colony Principle: A Methodology for Governed, Collaborative Agent Work
abstract: Large language models can plan, write code, operate tools, retrieve information, and carry out multi-step work. Those capabilities alone do not make an agent system dependable. This working paper presents the Colony Principle: a methodology for governed, long-horizon agent work that treats models as specialized, fallible participants in a durable execution substrate. The substrate, rather than a model session, owns continuity, shared work state, authority, effect status, evidence, recovery, and accountable learning. The paper defines four principles: Continuity, Collaboration, Consequence, and Evidence...together with observable public contracts, a bounded threat model, and an evaluation framework. Morchea is an implementation of this methodology. This is a public engineering methodology and position paper; it does not report aggregate benchmark results, claim formal certification, or disclose proprietary implementation details.

title: Doulita Token Compressor: Geometric Context Compression for LLMs - Research Preview. Duqueana Core
abstract: Doulita Token Compressor es un componente de investigación del ecosistema Duqueana Core diseñado para reducir el tamaño del contexto que se prepara antes de enviarlo a un modelo de lenguaje. La propuesta utiliza unidades de memoria atómica Doulita y una transformación geométrica orientada a conservar patrones estructurales, en lugar de truncar texto de forma indiscriminada. La demostración ejecutada que acompaña este informe generó 1.000 registros, con una entrada de 71.889 caracteres y una estimación de aproximadamente 17.972 tokens originales. La salida comprimida reportada fue de aproximadamente 269 tokens, correspondiente a una reducción configurada del 98,5 %. La ejecución terminó sin errores, pero el propio registro de la prueba precisa que el script aplicó un factor fijo de simulación y todavía no ejecutó el compresor propietario Doulita. Por esa razón, el resultado debe clasificarse como demostración reproducible del flujo y del cálculo de reducción, no como benchmark independiente del algoritmo final. evidence.title: Doulita Token Compressor: Geometric Context Compression for LLMs - Research Preview. Duqueana Core
evidence.abstract: Doulita Token Compressor es un componente de investigación del ecosistema Duqueana Core diseñado para reducir el tamaño del contexto que se prepara antes de enviarlo a un modelo de lenguaje. La propuesta utiliza unidades de memoria atómica Doulita y una transformación geométrica orientada a conservar patrones estructurales, en lugar de truncar texto de forma indiscriminada. La demostración ejecutada que acompaña este informe generó 1.000 registros, con una entrada de 71.889 caracteres y una estimación de aproximadamente 17.972 tokens originales. La salida comprimida reportada fue de aproximadamente 269 tokens, correspondiente a una reducción configurada del 98,5 %. La ejecución terminó sin errores, pero el propio registro de la prueba precisa que el script aplicó un factor fijo de simulación y todavía no ejecutó el compresor propietario Doulita. Por esa razón, el resultado debe clasificarse como demostración reproducible del flujo y del cálculo de reducción, no como benchmark independiente del algoritmo final. title: TRANSFORMING MARKETING ANALYTICS THROUGH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: ENHANCING CONSUMER INSIGHTS AND BUSINESS DECISION-MAKING
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has quickly changed the dynamics of the developing digital world and is connected to customers' strategic choices and competitive character. Predictive marketing's development has improved customer decision-making comprehension. This research investigates how artificial intelligence (AI) may improve marketing analytics, consumer segmentation, real-time decision-making, customer engagement, and operational efficiency. Additionally, it showcases the real-world uses of AI in a variety of sectors, such as chatbots, sentiment analysis, recommendation systems, and predictive modelling. According to the study's findings, AI greatly boosts consumer happiness, increases marketing efficacy, and gives businesses a long-term competitive edge. However, ethical AI techniques, high-quality data, and ongoing technical adaptability are necessary for effective application..

title: Делая мышление и возможности видимыми: модель когнитивной видимости, опосредованной искусственным интеллектом
abstract: В концептуальном препринте представлена модель когнитивной видимости, опосредованной искусственным интеллектом, — AI-Mediated Cognitive Visibility Model (AICVM). Она описывает, как повторяющийся диалог с генеративным ИИ может помочь человеку увидеть устойчивые особенности собственного мышления, заметить привычное самообесценивание, сформулировать зарождающиеся теории, расширить круг доступных представлению действий и определить осуществимый следующий шаг за пределами привычной модели жизни. Модель включает семь взаимосвязанных компонентов: скрытая когнитивная структура, фильтр самообесценивания, диалогическая экстернализация, возвращение выявленного паттерна, узнавание и пересмотр ценности, расширение горизонта действия и проверка в реальной жизни. Она различает рефлексивное усиление и внушающее присвоение интерпретации и отвергает использование ответа ИИ как диагноза, откровения или авторитетного знания о человеке.

title: The Shortest Description: A Narrative Review of Information Compression, from Huffman's Codes to Universal Prediction
abstract: Compression is information theory's applied heart: the art of the shortest description—David Huffman's 1952 minimum-redundancy codes, the Ziv–Lempel dictionaries of 1977 and 1978, Welch's 1984 LZW, the arithmetic coding of Rissanen and Langdon's 1981 and Witten, Neal, and Cleary's 1987, and the universal prediction whose theory Solomonoff's 1964 induction, Rissanen's 1978 minimum description length, and Hutter's 2005 universal intelligence tied compression to learning itself. This article presents a narrative review of the primary literature of that art, from Shannon's 1948 source coding theorem through the works above, Bell, Cleary, and Witten's 1990 Text Compression, and Salomon's 2007 Data Compression. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the codes' founding, in which the source's entropy became the limit and Huffman's tree approached it; the dictionaries' and arithmetics' eras, in which the Lempel–Ziv family and the arithmetic coders compressed without models' assumptions; and the universal settlement, in which induction's formal theory and the MDL principle made compression learning's measure. It is concluded that compression's history is the entropy bound's conquest—and that the learning-as-compression thesis is the field's deepest export to artificial intelligence.

title: Tracing Generated Samples to Training-Data Clusters in Flow-Matching Models
abstract: Understanding which training samples influence a generated image is an important problem in generative modeling. In flow matching, training samples influence the generated image through the velocity field along the generation trajectory. Removing samples to examine their counterfactual influence changes the velocity field, and the resulting effect on the final image depends on how the change propagates through the trajectory. Consequently, local changes in the velocity field do not necessarily predict the final counterfactual effect. This work investigates attribution in flow-matching models through a hybrid analytical--learned approach, and uses it to derive trajectory-based attribution scores at the cluster level. We evaluate these attribution scores using independently retrained leave-one-cluster-out (LOCO) models, and compare with several attribution baselines using two different flow-matching latent spaces. Our experiments show that semantic similarity constitutes a strong baseline, while the closed-form trajectory-based attribution is competitive in some metrics without requiring counterfactual retraining or model gradients. Our results show that attribution in flow matching depends not only on semantic similarity to training samples, but also on the latent representation, trajectory dynamics, and how influence is propagated to the final output.

title: Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians
abstract: This paper gives a survey of propositional modal logic in an intuitionistic setting. Mainly intended for readers already familiar with classical modal logic, we discuss why there are two prominent families of such logics, intuitionistic modal logics (IMLs) and constructive modal logics (CMLs), what motivates their study, and how they compare with each other. We then take a look at the logics lying between the CML and IML traditions, and survey various extensions and $\Diamond$/$\Box$-free fragments. We further record several observations which seem to be implicit or absent in the literature; we point out a small defect in the original semantics for $\textbf{CK}$ and prove Lyndon interpolation theorems for $\textbf{CK}$ and $\textbf{WK}$.

We further record several observations which seem to be implicit or absent in the literature; we point out a small defect in the original semantics for $\textbf{CK}$ and prove Lyndon interpolation theorems for $\textbf{CK}$ and $\textbf{WK}$.

title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Framework with Cross-Model Feature Stability Analysis for Heart Disease Prediction
abstract: Machine learning models for heart disease prediction are typically compared on discrimination alone, and the feature importances of a single selected model are then reported as though they described the data rather than the model.This paper develops an interpretable framework in which cross-model agreement is treated as a measurable quantity rather than an assumption. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) are trained on the Cleveland heart disease dataset, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) are computed for every model at both the cohort and the individual-patient level. A Feature Stability Score (FSS) is used to combine the three attribution profiles into a single ranking. We show analytically and empirically that the variance-based form of this score, FSS = 1 -σ², is not scale-invariant and is therefore confounded with importance itself: across the thirteen predictors its rank correlation with mean importance is ρ = -0.973, so the least important feature is scored as the most stable, and the resulting composite ranking correlates with raw importance at ρ = +0.995 -the stability term changes essentially nothing. We propose a scale-invariant reformulation based on the coefficient of variation of per-model normalised attributions, under which stability becomes an independent signal (ρ = +0.703) and the ranking changes materially: oldpeak rises from seventh to fourth while sex, chol, and age fall, the latter because Logistic Regression and XGBoost disagree about it by a factor of thirty. Random Forest attains the best discrimination (accuracy 0.8361, ROC-AUC 0.9188). At the individual level the three models disagree sharply on a representative patient, returning probabilities of 0.4987, 0.6224, and 0.1995 and splitting on the resulting decision, while the patient-level feature ranking diverges from the cohort ranking (ρ = 0.698, with eleven of thirteen positions changed). These results indicate that a single-model explanation of a heart disease classifier is not sufficient evidence about the underlying predictors.

title: A Quantum-Inspired Adaptive Intelligence Framework for Next-Generation Predictive Systems
abstract: Predictive systems face increasing complexity and volatility challenges in modern business environments, with traditional methods struggling to adapt without costly retraining. This research introduces a Quantum-Inspired Adaptive Intelligence Framework (QIAIF) that bridges quantum computing principles with classical machine learning to overcome these limitations. The framework leverages quantum-inspired tensor networks for dimensionality reduction, adaptive entanglement-based feature selection, and non- Euclidean representation learning to achieve unprecedented accuracy and computational efficiency. Validated using the public Walmart M5 Forecasting dataset, QIAIF demonstrated a 32.7% accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art deep learning models while reducing computational latency by 59.2%. Most notably, the framework achieved continuous performance improvements under distribution shifts without explicit retraining, recovering from market disruptions within 8 days compared to 21+ days for traditional approaches. These results establish a new direction for predictive intelligence by applying quantum-inspired computational principles to classical systems, with implications for large-scale retail forecasting environments.

title: Risk-Calibrated Semantic Navigation Under Distribution Shift: Confirmatory Core Dataset
abstract: Confirmatory core evidence for a preregistered ROS 2/Gazebo study of calibrated semantic navigation under controlled distribution shift. The archive contains the frozen 6,840-row manifest, 6,840 immutable episode summaries, process logs, exclusion and recovery records, derived analysis artifacts, and exact dependency lock needed to regenerate the reported H1-H4 results. Twenty prespecified infrastructure-invalid rows leave 6,820 analyzed episodes. H1 calibration and H3 clean-SPL noninferiority are supported; H2 collision reduction and H4 severity interaction are unsupported. Protocol v2.2 discloses three automatic reexecutions after non-durable pre-reboot writes, with a mandatory matched-stratum sensitivity that leaves all decisions unchanged. The scientific scope is simulation-only, with three protected Gazebo maps and a lightweight diagonal-Gaussian pixel classifier. It does not establish production-grade semantic perception or physical-robot safety. The optional 1.01 TB retained MCAP corpus is not part of this core deposit.

title: The Fragile Edge: A Narrative Review of Adversarial Machine Learning from Intriguing Properties to Certified Robustness
abstract: Adversarial machine learning---the science of how learned models fail by design---began as a curiosity of deep networks' blind spots and became a discipline that reshaped security, evaluation, and the theory of what classifiers learn. This article presents a narrative review of that arc's canonical line: Szegedy and colleagues' 2014 intriguing properties, Goodfellow, Shlens, and Szegedy's 2015 explaining and harnessing, Nguyen, Yosinski, and Clune's 2015 fooling images, Moosavi-Dezfooli, Fawzi, and Frossard's 2016 DeepFool, Papernot and colleagues' 2017 practical black-box attacks, Carlini and Wagner's 2017 robustness evaluation, Madry and colleagues' 2018 resistant models, Biggio and Roli's 2018 wild patterns survey, Akhtar and Mian's 2018 threat survey, Hendrycks and Dietterich's 2019 common corruptions benchmark, Tsipras and colleagues' 2019 robustness-accuracy tension, and Cohen, Rosenfeld, and Kolter's 2019 certified robustness. The review is organized around three themes: discovery, in which the linear lens and the fooling images revealed the models' brittleness; arms race, in which attacks sharpened, transferred, and went black-box while adversarial training answered; and consolidation, in which benchmarks, surveys, trade-off theorems, and randomized certification turned surprise into measurement. It is concluded that adversarial machine learning is the field's mirror---the discipline that forces learning's claims to face their worst cases---and that its lessons now underwrite the deployment of every safety-critical model.
